paragraphs: On Thursday, a teenager from another country visited the Explorers in the school library. She was a guest in the town for two weeks. Teacher Kim asked her to tell the children about her home. The guest had a blue backpack and a big map of her country. Her English was slow and clear. The room was quiet. The children sat on the floor, and Mia held the camera. "My home is far from here," said the guest, "but it is not so different."

First, she talked about the capital of her country. "It is a big city with a wide river," she said. "The buildings in the old part are made of pale stone." "In the morning, the sun makes them almost white." "There is also a tall clock, and it is very old." "Is it like our town?" asked Leo. "No, it is much bigger, and it has many trains," she said. Lily wrote two words in her notebook: pale stone.

Next, the guest told the children about sightseeing in the capital. "Visitors can go sightseeing by bus, by boat, or on foot," she said. "There are many bridges over the river, and each bridge has a story." "My favorite place is a big old market under a roof." "Are there animals in the city?" asked Mia. "Yes, many birds live in the park by the river," said the guest. Mia smiled and took a photo of the map.

After that, she talked about her family's farm in the countryside. "We grow wheat and apples, and we have a few cows," she said. "The ingredients for our bread all come from the farm." "The bread is made in a small oven every Sunday." "It is quiet there, and the hills are green." May asked, "What do you eat with the bread?" "We eat it with cheese and sweet red fruit," said the guest.

At the end, she took a paper out of her backpack. It was the recipe for her family's bread. "You can copy it, and you can make the bread at home," she said. May copied the recipe in her notebook, and Mia took a photo of the paper. Teacher Kim said, "We will make the bread on a Saturday." Everybody clapped for the guest. Lily wrote the title for the blog: "A Guest from Another Country."
